title: Work IQ: federated connectors for governed access to more data sources
summary: Hold: Microsoft now documents automatic connector participation in Work IQ, with connector access enabled by default, and a tenant policy that can disable that participation. The briefing still calls the default unstated and the Work IQ-specific connector control undocumented. The existing connector paths, automation and licensing statements are otherwise supported.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans Work IQ federated connectors for governed access to additional enterprise data sources.
claims.quote: Enable Work IQ to use federated connectors for governed access to additional enterprise data sources.

claims.claim: The roadmap lists Microsoft Graph and Work IQ as products.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Graph", "Work IQ"]

claims.claim: The roadmap status remains In development even though Learn describes connector participation.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.claim: The roadmap target is November CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "November CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview target is October CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "October CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability and Preview release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated what Work IQ federated connector participation does on arrival.
claims.quote: Copilot Connectors configured in Microsoft 365 Copilot automatically participate in Work IQ APIs. ... Connector access is enabled by default.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to on. Replace 'Microsoft has not stated what this capability does on arrival.' with 'Microsoft documents connector access as enabled by default: configured connectors participate when available to the signed-in user and connected by that user in Copilot Chat; Work IQ must be enabled for the organisation.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/connectors-in-work-iq-apis.

claims.quote: You pay for use of the Work IQ API through a usage-based model that uses Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Work IQ API access is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing.
claims.quote: Work IQ API access is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing and available through usage-based billing.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Work IQ API usage is billed by usage through Copilot Credits, supporting the variable cost rating.
claims.quote: Work IQ cost is variable based on usage ... Work IQ API usage consumes Copilot Credits shared with other eligible services.

claims.claim: Copilot Credits consumed by Work IQ are shared with other eligible services.
claims.quote: Work IQ API usage consumes Copilot Credits shared with other eligible services.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Connector-backed Microsoft 365 tools have separate connector-specific licensing requirements.
claims.quote: Connector-backed Microsoft 365 tools | Connector licensing | Confirm the selected connector's prerequisites. A connector can require a Microsoft 365 Copilot license for each calling user.

claims.claim: Users querying federated Copilot connector sources need a Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licence or Microsoft 365 E7.
claims.quote: Federated Copilot connectors are available only to tenants and users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license (or Microsoft 365 E7).

claims.claim: Work IQ API access through A2A, REST or MCP does not use connector licensing.
claims.quote: Work IQ API through A2A, REST, or MCP | Usage-based billing | Enable billing with Copilot Credits. This path doesn't use connector licensing.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Federated connectors use Model Context Protocol to fetch external data in real time.
claims.quote: Use Model Context Protocol (MCP) to fetch data in real time.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Federated connector access uses the user's identity and source permissions.
claims.quote: Access data using the user's identity and permissions.

claims.claim: Federated connectors do not index external data into Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: Don't index external data into Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Administrators manage federated connectors in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Are managed and governed by admins in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Learn describes connected enterprise sources as participating in Work IQ Copilot, entity and schema tools.
claims.quote: Connected enterprise sources participate in Work IQ Copilot, entity, and schema tools.

claims.claim: Connector developers must enable participation in Work IQ APIs.
claims.quote: Connector developers must enable participation in Work IQ APIs.
claims.fix: The Learn search excerpt supports this wording, but the opened overview now links to https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/connectors-in-work-iq-apis, which says participation is automatic. Replace the developer-enablement clause with 'Copilot Connectors configured in Microsoft 365 Copilot automatically participate in Work IQ APIs; participation may be limited by data sensitivity requirements or partner agreements.' Cite that page.

claims.claim: Federated connectors do not copy external data into Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: Federated connectors don't copy or store data in Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: The source system enforces permissions for federated connector access.
claims.quote: The source system enforces all permissions. Users can only access content they're authorized to view and make changes they're authorized to make in the original data source.

claims.claim: Live external source results are used in Copilot responses.
claims.quote: Copilot selects relevant connector tools at runtime and uses the live results returned by the source to respond in the conversation.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Where federated connectors expose appropriate tools, Copilot can create, update or delete data with user approval.
claims.quote: Can read data and, where a connector provides the tools, create, update, or delete data with the user's approval.

claims.claim: New write-capable connector tools default to Needs approval.
claims.quote: If a connector publisher adds a new write-capable tool or changes an existing one, the tool is set to Needs approval by default.

claims.claim: The Researcher agent remains read-only for federated connector access.
claims.quote: The Researcher agent doesn't support write, update, or delete actions. Federated Copilot connectors remain read-only in this experience.

claims.claim: The general Copilot connectors overview still describes federated connectors as read-only, unlike the federated overview's write-action documentation.
claims.quote: Write actions will be available starting early October 2026. ... Federated connectors are read-only; they can search and fetch content but can't write data back.

claims.claim: MCP servers with source-IP restrictions may need Microsoft 365 Copilot static egress IP allow-listing.
claims.quote: If your MCP server restricts incoming traffic by source IP address, configure its firewall to allow the static egress IP addresses used by Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.claim: Individual connectors can be enabled, disabled or staged at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Connectors > Your connections > connector > Enable / Disable / Staged rollout.
claims.quote: Enable / Disable | Copilot > Connectors > Your connections ... Staged rollout | Copilot > Connectors > Your connections > Staged rollout

claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.claim: Both block and unblock calls require delegated CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All permission.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account) | CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All | Not available.

claims.claim: The block and unblock calls are beta APIs not supported in production applications.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: The block and unblock operations do not configure a staged rollout audience.
claims.quote: Unblock a Copilot package to allow its usage. ... Don't supply a request body for this method.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no automation explicitly for federated connector staged rollout as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: federated connector staged rollout API Graph packages staging users groups; "federated connectors" "allowedUsersAndGroups"; connector availableTo staged. Opened staged-rollout, custom connector management and package update; no explicit federated staging mapping.

claims.claim: Blocking a custom federated connector has the same effect as disabling it.
claims.quote: Block (Agents > Tools) | Same as Disable.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/unblock allows use of a blocked package.
claims.quote: Unblock a Copilot package to allow its usage. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/unblock

claims.claim: Publisher-type connector access is configured at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access.
claims.quote: Agent and plugin access | Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access | Allows or blocks connectors in bulk by publisher type, including future connectors.

claims.claim: The preview beta POST configurationMonitors operation sets publisher-type access using mode applyOnce and microsoft.agent.allowedagenttypes with the named valueObject Boolean properties.
claims.quote: These resources also support remediation and applyOnce. ... areISVAppsAllowed ... areMicrosoftAppsAllowed ... areTenantScopedAppsAllowed ... "resourceType": "microsoft.agent.allowedagenttypes"

claims.claim: The signed-in administrator needs the AI Administrator role for Agent resource applyOnce changes.
claims.quote: AI Administrator is the least-privileged role for the signed-in user for remediation and applyOnce; don't assign that user-role requirement to the service principal.

claims.claim: Connector user access is configured at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > User access.
claims.quote: Plugins include tools, MCP servers, connectors, skills, and other AI artifacts. ... Select Agents > Settings > User access to manage your organization's agents and plugins.

claims.claim: The preview beta POST configurationMonitors operation sets User access with mode applyOnce and microsoft.agent.useraccess using valueObject.userAssignmentCategory as everyone or noOne.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors ... mode ... monitorOnly, applyOnce, unknownFutureValue ... An active applyOnce monitor runs in the background on behalf of the signed-in administrator and then becomes inactive.

claims.claim: The documented User access applyOnce schema provides everyone or noOne, not specific-group assignment.
claims.quote: userAssignmentCategory | Write | String | Specifies whether all users or no users can access agents and plugins. | everyone, noOne

claims.claim: The app calling TCM applyOnce needs delegated ConfigurationMonitoring.ReadWrite.All permission.
claims.quote: Creating an applyOnce monitor supports delegated permissions only. In addition to the calling app's delegated ConfigurationMonitoring.ReadWrite.All permission, the TCM service principal needs delegated permissions for the target workloads

claims.claim: The TCM service principal needs delegated CopilotPolicySettings.ReadWrite for Agent resource applyOnce changes.
claims.quote: For remediation and applyOnce, grant it the CopilotPolicySettings.ReadWrite delegated permission.

claims.claim: Tenant Work IQ MCP policy is accessible at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Policy.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Agents > Tools. ... In the tools registry, select Work IQ MCP. ... On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.

claims.claim: The Work IQ MCP Policy tab is shown when available.
claims.quote: On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy changes can take up to 24 hours to apply.
claims.quote: After you save the setting, it can take up to 24 hours for the policy change to apply across your tenant.

claims.claim: An API operation for turning tenant Work IQ MCP policy on or off is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP tenant policy configuration API; "Work IQ" "policy" "PATCH"; "Work IQ MCP" policy API copilot update. Opened policy-governance-mcp, package overview/update and TCM Agent resources; no operation sets this policy.

claims.quote: Work IQ MCP provides Rego-based policy governance to control access to connectors through Work IQ APIs. ... Administrators can explicitly enable or disable connector participation in Work IQ paths through tenant-level policies.
claims.fix: Remove the both-null 'Work IQ-specific control for federated connectors' row. In the existing Work IQ MCP policy row's note, replace 'General Work IQ MCP control.' with 'Tenant policy can explicitly enable or disable connector participation in Work IQ paths.' claims.claim: Copilot Chat users approve individual write tools, and Always allow and Allow for conversation apply to a tool rather than an entire connector.
